pairings.why: The pair a portalled panel ACTUALLY paints. Tier 3, where the rest of this table is tier 2, and deliberately so: a portalled surface resolves its background against the portal scope and, with no declared colour, its text against the page - which shipped 1.26:1 in dark theme. Declaring only the tier 2 ancestors is not equivalent; repointing a tier 3 fg to a DIFFERENT tier 2 alias measured 3.10:1 in light with every gate green, because nothing measured the pair the component paints.

The listbox cursor bar against the TINT it is actually drawn on. An inset box-shadow paints over the element's OWN background, so `option-bg-active` is the adjacency the bar abuts along its full height - and the first fix pinned it against the PANEL instead, which is the more permissive of the two. Measured: repointing option-cursor to {color.border.default} sat at 2.72:1 light and 2.36:1 dark against the tint with every gate green. Two seats found it independently. Both adjacencies are declared now rather than whichever one looked right.

The check glyph, which is the SOLE visible carrier of the selected choice since the `--selected` class was removed for carrying no CSS rule. That removal is what made this token load-bearing, and it was enrolled in no contrast gate at all: repointing option-check-fg to {color.bg.surface} made the check invisible - screenshot-confirmed - with check:contrast, check:component-css and 1283 tests green. Declared against BOTH the panel and the active row's tint, because the glyph sits on either depending on the row.
